definitions.explanation: A long-handled cup or spoon used for scooping and pouring water or other liquids. Found at Shinto shrines and Buddhist temples for ritual hand-washing, and used in traditional Japanese settings.

examples.japanese: {柄杓|ひしゃく}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{水|みず}→水：02258_mizu⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦すくう→すくう：09994_sukuu⟧。
examples.english: To scoop water with a ladle.

examples.japanese: ⟦{神社|じんじゃ}→神社：01620_jinja⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{手水舎|ちょうずや}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧{柄杓|ひしゃく}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{使|つか}って→使う：00473_tsukau⟧⟦{手|て}→手：00569_te⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{清|きよ}める→清める：13340_kiyomeru⟧。
examples.english: At the purification fountain of a shrine, you use a dipper to cleanse your hands.

examples.japanese: ⟦{竹|たけ}→竹：02220_take⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{作|つく}られた→作る：00481_tsukuru⟧{柄杓|ひしゃく}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{茶室|ちゃしつ}→茶室：14081_chashitsu⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{前|まえ}→前：02255_mae⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{置|お}かれていて→置く：01092_oku⟧、⟦{風情|ふぜい}→風情：09057_fuzei⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{感|かん}じた→感じる：02044_kanjiru⟧。
examples.english: A bamboo ladle was placed in front of the tea room, giving a sense of rustic elegance.

notes:
Also written in hiragana as ひしゃく. The {柄杓|ひしゃく} is most familiar to visitors of Japanese shrines and temples, where it is used at the {手水舎|ちょうずや} (purification fountain) to wash hands and rinse the mouth before entering the sacred area. It also plays a role in the tea ceremony (⟦{茶道|さどう}→茶道：04451_sadou⟧).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {柄杓|ひしゃく}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{水|みず}→水：02258_mizu⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦すくう→すくう：09994_sukuu⟧: to scoop water with a ladle
- ⟦{竹|たけ}→竹：02220_take⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{柄杓|ひしゃく}: bamboo dipper
- {柄杓|ひしゃく}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{持|も}つ→持つ：00478_motsu⟧: to hold a ladle
- {手水|ちょうず}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{柄杓|ひしゃく}: the dipper at a purification fountain

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦おたま→おたま：04471_otama⟧ / お{玉杓子|たまじゃくし}: ladle (for cooking) — the round ladle used in the kitchen for soups and stews
- しゃもじ: rice paddle — a flat spatula for serving rice
- {杓子|しゃくし}: ladle; scoop — a broader term; {柄杓|ひしゃく} is a specific type with a long handle

CULTURAL NOTE:
During the COVID-19 pandemic, many shrines removed their {柄杓|ひしゃく} from {手水舎|ちょうずや} for hygiene reasons, replacing them with flowing water systems. Some have since restored them.
